fields.mechanism: Closed‑system technologies that isolate the fluid pathway to reduce contamination risk.
fields.intervention: Incorporate a needle‑free, hermetically sealed port with a self‑sealing membrane at the catheter hub, creating a closed fluid circuit that eliminates open lumens during dialysis connections.
fields.expected_effect: Maintains catheter flow patency for ≥8 weeks by minimizing fibrin sheath formation and thrombus development due to reduced exposure to contaminants.
fields.falsification_test: Conduct a randomized trial comparing standard hubs versus the sealed needle‑free ports; record time to first flow‑patency loss over 8 weeks—significantly longer patency with the sealed design falsifies the hypothesis that the intervention has no effect.

fields.mechanism: Closed‑system (needle‑free) port technology that reduces external contamination risk, thereby limiting fibrin sheath and thrombus formation.

fields.mechanism: Closed-system needle‑free port that creates a sealed fluidic pathway while employing antimicrobial material science to inhibit biofilm and fibrin sheath formation.
fields.intervention: Integrate a needle‑free, hermetically sealed port with an inner lumen coated in a slow‑release antimicrobial polymer into the tunneled hemodialysis catheter tip, eliminating external fluid entry and chemically suppressing coagulation/fibrin deposition.
fields.expected_effect: Sustained lumen patency for ≥8 weeks by preventing blood‑air interface‑driven coagulation and inhibiting microbial‑induced fibrin sheath formation, thus maintaining flow without additional flushing.
fields.falsification_test: Conduct a randomized controlled trial comparing standard catheters to the hybrid sealed‑antimicrobial catheters; primary endpoint is time to ≥30 % flow reduction or need for flushing over an 8‑week period, with ultrasound verification of fibrin sheath presence.
